dossier.architecture: Compact turret fed by rotating floor/conical spindexer and curved-rack collection.

subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve; exact module specification unresolved in reviewed team replies.
subsystems.intake: Third collector version adds kicker and articulated secondary kicker; curved rack stays low in stow to preserve capacity.
subsystems.transfer: Cone and rotating floor; separate X44s power spindexer and uptake. Ratios and feeder wheels revised repeatedly; automated recovery clears intermittent jams.
subsystems.scoring: Three-X44 flywheel, no powered top roller; compact turret and hood. Team identifies light printed wheel plus supplemental inertia kit.
subsystems.endgame: Endgame installation not established in reviewed release.
subsystems.controls: Empirically tuned tables plus iterative physics solution compensate motion and spin; local floodlight helps close-range tag shadows, not distant detection.

versions: At least three intake configurations; feed-wheel changes reported seven/eight times.
Do not treat speculative third-party explanations in thread as team-confirmed geometry.
dossier.analysis: A conical spindexer is a different singulation family from a pocketed DYE Rotor. Curved deployment preserves low internal volume; contact friction, congestion and turret interference remain the transfer-critical variables.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2026-9483 · Small turret throughput cannot be inferred from exterior geometry
context_documents.body:
# 2026-9483: Small turret throughput cannot be inferred from exterior geometry

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

First-party replies describe separate X44s for indexer and spindexer, a spinning floor/cone with no deliberate wall compression, and multiple feeder-wheel and ratio trials. The third intake version adds a kicker and movable secondary kicker. The shooter lacks an upper roller; its moving-shot solution combines tuned lookup data and a physics calculation that compensates for spin.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team says the movable kicker resolves earlier collector difficulty and clarifies that the feeder delivers fuel without spin. It does not provide a definitive causal explanation for all of the achieved spindexer throughput. The added flood light helps close-range tag reliability rather than substantially increasing long-range detection.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

The absence of a counter-roller makes spin an explicit aiming input rather than something to assume away. A compact turret may leave more free hopper area, but the detailed explanation of dead zones and geometry offered by another commenter is expressly an outsider’s hypothesis. Keep that hypothesis separate from the team’s replies. Successful self-unjamming also does not mean jams never occur; the source explicitly acknowledges occasional jams.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure entrance spin and moving-shot error across turret angles, record jam/recovery frequency and time, and inspect exact CAD before copying clearances or interpreting an image-based diameter estimate.

## Limits

Selected first-party replies 26, 30, 33, 35 and 47 in topic 515383. Reply 44 is outside analysis, not team intent or a CAD inspection.
